sections.html:
The Florida homestead exemption takes up to $50,000 off the assessed value of your home before tax is figured. It comes in two layers. Layer one is $25,000 and hits every levy, schools too. Layer two is another $25,000, but it only covers assessed value over $50,000 and never touches school taxes.

The second layer moves with inflation. When the CPI change is positive, the amount is adjusted each January 1. When it is negative, the amount holds steady. The state's table starts from a 2024 base, so read your own bill or phone the appraiser for the figure now in force.

All it does is shrink the taxable base. Each taxing district's millage still applies to the value that remains.

sections.h2: Who qualifies and what ends it
sections.html:
To qualify you hold title on January 1 and also live there as a permanent resident by that date. One permanent residence per owner.

Three things end it:

  • You rent the home out.
  • The house stops being your permanent home.
  • You stop being a Florida permanent resident.

Servicemembers have an exception under s. 196.061 that lets them lease the home without giving up homestead. Anyone else who moves away should tell the appraiser, so an exemption you no longer qualify for does not stay on the roll.

sections.h2: How to apply, and what to do if you are denied
sections.html:
Send Form DR-501 to your county property appraiser. Exemption and agricultural classification claims close on March 1.

Once a denial letter arrives you have 30 days to petition the value adjustment board. Fighting the value itself is a different track: a DR-486 petition goes to the clerk of court within 25 days after the August Notice of Proposed Property Taxes.

Eligibility is the appraiser's call. Bills come from the tax collector. When a problem could belong to either, call the appraiser first.

Save Our Homes slows the yearly climb in a homestead's assessed value. Past year one, the rise is held to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller, and assessed value can never pass just value.

sections.h2: What happens to the cap when you sell
sections.html:
Years of built-up protection end at sale. Foreclosure and any transfer of legal or beneficial title count as a change of ownership too, and the following January 1 the parcel is reset to just value. Spouse-to-spouse transfers and certain transfers at death are exceptions.

The exemption does not travel either. A buyer who moves in files a new claim, and one who rents it out cannot claim at all. After many years of ownership, the new owner's first full bill can run far above yours.

A closing in spring or summer still falls in a tax year whose assessment was fixed the previous January, and the November bill is split under the purchase contract. Read that clause before you sign.

sections.h2: Moving the savings to another house
sections.html:
Portability can move your Save Our Homes savings to a new Florida homestead, if you beat the clock. You have three years to establish the new homestead, counted from January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, not from closing day. Form DR-501T goes in with the DR-501.

Section 193.155(8) cuts the new home's assessed value by $500,000 or by the old home's just-minus-assessed difference, whichever is less. Changes made by ch. 2026-239 start with the 2027 roll, so confirm with the appraiser which rules cover your move.

sections.h2: Extra breaks for seniors, service members and disabled owners
sections.html:
More relief can stack on the base exemption. Some of it depends on a local vote.

  • Age 65 and up: a local ordinance can add as much as $50,000 for households under an income limit that started at $20,000 and is indexed by CPI (s. 196.075(2)).
  • 65 and older, 25 years a permanent resident, just value below $250,000: an ordinance may exempt the whole assessed value, income limit permitting.
  • Military retirees 65 and older with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount matching the VA disability percentage, which passes to an unremarried surviving spouse (s. 196.082).
  • Former servicemembers with a disability rating of 10 percent or more: $5,000 off assessed value (ss. 196.081, 196.091).
  • Total and permanent service-connected disability: the homestead may be fully exempt.

Your appraiser can tell you which ones your county offers.

You can defer some of the tax. Form DR-570 has to reach the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. What you can defer is the tax above 5 percent of last year's household income, or all of it if income is below $10,000. Permanent residents 65 and older can defer whatever exceeds 3 percent of income.

Paying instead? Discounts shrink month by month: 4 percent for November, 3 in December, 2 in January, 1 in February. April 1 is when unpaid tax turns delinquent, and tax certificates go on sale by June 1.

Ask the tax collector for a payoff figure before you list, so any deferral lien on the home is cleared at closing.

sections.h2: Checklist before you list a homestead
sections.html:
Start with the parcel record on the appraiser's site, which lists assessed value, just value and exemption status. The distance between the two values is what Save Our Homes has kept off your bill.

  • Confirm your current exemption application was accepted.
  • Note any senior, veteran or disability benefit. None of them transfers to a buyer.
  • Find out whether a DR-570 deferral is on record.
  • Decide early whether you plan to port the benefit, because that starts a three year window.

Hand your answers to the closing agent so the buyer can plan a new filing.

Pull your last two tax bills as well. Compare the line for each taxing body, since school, county and city rates differ, and a buyer's agent will probably do the same. Seeing which levies the exemption actually reduces shows whether the buyer's real cost after reassessment will be close to yours or far above it. If you remodeled recently, ask the appraiser whether the new improvements were added to the roll, because additions can raise just value on their own.

A cash buyer skips the lender's escrow setup and appraisal timeline, but the reassessment still happens the following January 1 either way.

faqs.q: When must a Florida homestead claim be filed?
faqs.a: By March 1, with the county appraiser, using Form DR-501. You must have made the home your permanent residence by January 1. A denial goes to the value adjustment board, and that petition has a 30 day window from the mailing of the denial letter.

faqs.q: How big is the Florida homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Up to $50,000 in assessed value. The first $25,000 offsets all taxes, school levies included. The extra $25,000 touches only value above $50,000 and excludes school taxes, and it is indexed to inflation.

faqs.q: Does a buyer inherit my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, and the parcel returns to just value the following January 1. Spouse transfers and certain transfers at death are among the exceptions.

faqs.q: Can I keep my cap savings when I buy elsewhere in Florida?
faqs.a: Often, through portability. Establish the new homestead within three years counted from January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, and file DR-501T with DR-501. The reduction cannot exceed $500,000 or the old home's just-minus-assessed gap, whichever is lower.

faqs.q: What if I rent my homestead out?
faqs.a: Renting costs you the exemption, as does moving away or leaving Florida as a permanent resident. Servicemembers are the exception under s. 196.061.
